title: Monitoring Athlete Training Loads: Consensus Statement
authors: Bourdon PC, Cardinale M, Murray A, Gastin P, Kellmann M, Varley MC, Gabbett TJ, Coutts AJ, Burgess DJ, Gregson W, Cable NT
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Expert consensus from the February 2016 Doha conference on monitoring athlete training loads
findings: The statement brings together key findings and recommendations from a February 2016 conference in Doha on monitoring athlete training loads, in a shared conceptual framework for coaches and sport-science staff.
It outlines what load monitoring is, how it is applied in research and practice, why it matters and where it is heading.
The abstract refers to quantifying both internal and external loads to help protect athletes from injury and ill health; it reports no numeric thresholds.
Brings together key findings and recommendations from the 2016 Doha conference into a shared conceptual framework for coaches and sport-science and -medicine staff.
Outlines what athlete-load monitoring is, how it is applied in research and practice, why it matters (rationale and goals) and where it is heading.
The abstract refers to quantifying both internal and external loads placed on athletes.
limitations: Conference-based expert consensus with no systematic methods described in the abstract; no thresholds; applicability to a single recreational runner is by analogy; full-text recommendations not read.
implications: Use the internal/external-load framework to structure what the app records; combine measures rather than rely on one number.
Frame load features as decision support for one athlete, not validated injury predictors; no parameter value is justified by the abstract.
Record external load (distance, pace, time) and internal load (HR, RPE) for each session and keep them as separate model inputs.
No numeric rule is justified from this abstract.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, IJSPP, Apr 2017, first author Bourdon, 11 authors. Removed 'developed largely from team-sport contexts' from limitations because the abstract does not say so.
